INCIDENT REPORT: PAYMENT SERVICE OUTAGE

**Report ID:** INC-2024-0415-003
**Date:** 15 April 2024
**Classification:** FINAL
**Status:** Archived — Historical Record (supersedes preliminary notes circulated via email on 15 April 2024)

---

**1. OVERVIEW**

At approximately 09:42 AEST on Monday 15 April 2024, the Payment Service (Payments) began returning elevated error rates for authorisation and capture requests. The degradation was detected by automated alerting and subsequently confirmed by the on-call engineer. The service remained in a degraded state for a period of approximately two hours and fourteen minutes before returning to normal operations at 11:56 AEST. No customer funds were lost, however a subset of transactions were declined during the incident window and required manual retry by merchants. This report documents the incident, its impact, and the actions taken to resolve it.

**2. SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION**

Payment Service has_severity_level SEV2 level. Record status: historical. This classification was applied by the Incident Commander at 09:55 AEST and retained for the duration of the incident. The SEV2 designation was based on the partial loss of a core payment function affecting a measurable segment of live traffic, without complete service unavailability or confirmed financial data compromise.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Severity Level | SEV2 |
| Incident Commander | M. Okafor |
| On-Call Engineer (Primary) | J. Whitfield |
| On-Call Engineer (Secondary) | R. Singh |
| SRE Lead | T. Nguyen |
| Status Page Updated | Yes — 09:58 AEST |

**3. IMPACT ASSESSMENT**

**3.1 Customer-Facing Impact**

During the incident window, approximately 4.2% of authorisation requests failed with a 503 response code. A further 1.8% of requests experienced latency exceeding the 5-second threshold and were terminated by the client. Affected merchants observed declined transactions at point-of-sale and through e-commerce checkouts. No erroneous duplicate charges or double debits were reported. A small number of merchants (fewer than 20) contacted support regarding declined transactions; all were advised that the issue was under investigation and that retries would be required.

**3.2 Internal Impact**

The Payments service consumed 100% of its allocated database connection pool for a period of approximately 45 minutes. This caused a knock-on effect on the reporting and reconciliation jobs that share the same database cluster. These jobs were delayed by up to 90 minutes but completed without data loss. The internal admin portal also experienced intermittent timeouts during the peak of the incident.

**3.3 Data Integrity**

No data corruption or loss was identified. The transaction journal remained consistent. A post-incident reconciliation check (completed at 14:30 AEST) confirmed that all transactions processed before and after the incident are accounted for. No manual correction entries were required.

**4. TIMELINE OF EVENTS**

All times are AEST (UTC+10). The timeline below has been compiled from alert history, incident channel logs, and engineer notes. Times are approximate where noted.

**5. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (PRELIMINARY)**

The feature flag controlling the new code path was disabled at 10:47 AEST to mitigate the incident. The underlying code change has been reverted from the main branch pending further review and the addition of a database migration to create the required index.
| Time (AEST) | Action |
|---|---|
| 09:58 | Incident declared; status page updated |
| 10:02 | On-call engineers identified connection pool exhaustion from dashboards |
| 10:11 | Database team engaged to inspect query performance |
| 10:23 | Missing index confirmed via query plan analysis |
| 10:47 | Feature flag disabled; traffic reverted to previous code path |
| 10:52 | Connection pool utilisation returned to baseline (below 40%) |
| 11:05 | All queued requests drained; error rate returned to 0% |
| 11:08 | Status page updated to "Monitoring" |
| 12:30 | Status page updated to "Resolved" |

The database migration to add the required index has been written and is undergoing review. It will be applied during the next scheduled maintenance window after approval from the database team. The migration has been tested against a production snapshot and completes in approximately 6 minutes without locking the table.

**7. ACTION ITEMS**

| Action | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Add index to transactions table (migration M-2024-04-15-01) | D. Okafor (DB) | 2024-04-16 | In progress |
| Update deployment automation to respect manual rollout flags | J. Whitfield | 2024-04-17 | Not started |
| Add a pre-deployment check for missing indexes in staging | R. Singh | 2024-04-19 | Not started |
| Add a dashboard alert for connection pool utilisation >80% for 5 minutes | T. Nguyen | 2024-04-16 | In progress |
| Review feature flag defaults in the release checklist | M. Chen | 2024-04-18 | Not started |
| Conduct a full post-incident review with the payments team | T. Nguyen | 2024-04-22 | Scheduled |

**8. POST-INCIDENT REVIEW NOTES**

The incident review will be held on 2024-04-22 at 14:00 AEST in the SRE meeting room (or via video conference for remote attendees). The agenda will cover the timeline, root cause, and action items listed above. All participants from the incident are expected to attend or provide written updates beforehand.

Payment Service has_incident_id INC-2024-04-15 identifier. Record status: historical.

Key discussion points to be covered:

- Whether the staging environment should more closely mirror production data volumes. The current staging database contains approximately 200,000 rows in the transactions table, which is not sufficient to expose query performance issues.
- Whether the deployment automation should require a manual confirmation step when a feature flag is set to "enabled" for 100% of traffic.
- Whether the SRE team should have visibility of the release notes for changes that affect database queries. Currently, the release notes are reviewed by the payments team only.
- Whether the alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation should be lowered to 70% to provide earlier warning.

**9. ATTACHMENTS**

| Attachment | Description |
|---|---|
| Attachment 1: Alert history export (09:40–11:10 AEST) | Raw alerts from the monitoring system |
| Attachment 2: Query plan analysis (10:23 AEST) | Output from the database team's investigation |
| Attachment 3: Deployment log for release v2.14.1 | Automation logs showing the feature flag default |
| Attachment 4: Connection pool utilisation graph | Screenshot from the metrics dashboard |

**10. INCIDENT IDENTIFIER**

This incident has been recorded in the incident management system under the identifier INC-2024-04-15. All related documentation, alert history, and communication logs should reference this identifier when filing follow-up work or when querying the incident history. The incident record is accessible to all SRE team members and to the payments team leadership. The identifier has been used in the action items above where applicable, and the post-incident review minutes will reference it as well.
**10. INCIDENT IDENTIFIER** (continued)

The incident identifier INC-2024-04-15 has been propagated to the following systems: the alert management platform (alert group `payments-prod`), the change management record associated with release v2.14.1, and the on-call handover notes for the week commencing 15 April 2024. Any future correspondence regarding this incident should include the identifier in the subject line.

**11. POST-INCIDENT REVIEW MINUTES**

The post-incident review was held on 18 April 2024, 10:00–11:30 AEST, via video conference. Attendees: J. Okafor (Incident Commander), M. Tran (SRE Lead), A. Patel (Database Team), S. Nguyen (Payments Engineering), R. Whitfield (QA), and L. Chen (Product). The following minutes were recorded.

**11.1 Review of timeline**

The group confirmed the timeline as documented in Section 4. No discrepancies were raised. One attendee noted that the monitoring system's alert for connection pool utilisation fired at 09:41 AEST, which is approximately one minute after the pool reached saturation. The alert was acknowledged at 09:47 AEST by the on-call engineer.

**11.2 Root cause discussion**

The database team presented the query plan analysis (Attachment 2). The plan confirmed that the new query in release v2.14.1 performed a full table scan on the `transactions` table. The table contains approximately 4.8 million rows in production. The query was executed on every request when the feature flag was enabled, and the execution time was measured at 3.2 seconds under normal load. The connection pool had a maximum of 50 connections, and each request held a connection for the duration of the query. At the time of the incident, the pool was exhausted within 90 seconds of the flag being enabled.

The discussion then turned to the staging environment. The current staging database contains approximately 200,000 rows in the transactions table, which is not sufficient to expose query performance issues. The team agreed that this is a contributing factor to the lack of detection during pre-release testing.

**11.3 Feature flag process**

The deployment automation for release v2.14.1 was configured to set the feature flag to "enabled" for 100% of traffic as the default. The team discussed whether the automation should require a manual confirmation step when a feature flag is set to "enabled" for 100% of traffic. No decision was reached, but the action item was recorded as ACTION-5.

**11.4 Release notes visibility**

The payments team noted that the release notes for v2.14.1 were reviewed internally but were not shared with the SRE team. The release notes contained a description of the new query and its expected behaviour. The SRE team requested visibility of release notes for changes that affect database queries. The payments team agreed to circulate release notes to the SRE team for such changes. This will be tracked under ACTION-6.

**11.5 Alerting threshold**

The current alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation is 80%. The SRE team proposed lowering the threshold to 70% to provide earlier warning. The payments team expressed concern that a lower threshold might generate noise during normal peak usage. The matter was deferred to a follow-up meeting. The alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation is currently configured at 80% and no change has been applied as of the date of these minutes.

**11.6 Action items**

documents.title: Incident Report: Payment Service Outage
documents.content:
INCIDENT REPORT: PAYMENT SERVICE OUTAGE

**Report ID:** INC-2024-0415-003
**Date:** 15 April 2024
**Classification:** FINAL
**Status:** Archived — Historical Record (supersedes preliminary notes circulated via email on 15 April 2024)

---

**1. OVERVIEW**

At approximately 09:42 AEST on Monday 15 April 2024, the Payment Service (Payments) began returning elevated error rates for authorisation and capture requests. The degradation was detected by automated alerting and subsequently confirmed by the on-call engineer. The service remained in a degraded state for a period of approximately two hours and fourteen minutes before returning to normal operations at 11:56 AEST. No customer funds were lost, however a subset of transactions were declined during the incident window and required manual retry by merchants. This report documents the incident, its impact, and the actions taken to resolve it.

**2. SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION**

Payment Service has_severity_level SEV2 level. Record status: historical. This classification was applied by the Incident Commander at 09:55 AEST and retained for the duration of the incident. The SEV2 designation was based on the partial loss of a core payment function affecting a measurable segment of live traffic, without complete service unavailability or confirmed financial data compromise.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Severity Level | SEV2 |
| Incident Commander | M. Okafor |
| On-Call Engineer (Primary) | J. Whitfield |
| On-Call Engineer (Secondary) | R. Singh |
| SRE Lead | T. Nguyen |
| Status Page Updated | Yes — 09:58 AEST |

**3. IMPACT ASSESSMENT**

**3.1 Customer-Facing Impact**

During the incident window, approximately 4.2% of authorisation requests failed with a 503 response code. A further 1.8% of requests experienced latency exceeding the 5-second threshold and were terminated by the client. Affected merchants observed declined transactions at point-of-sale and through e-commerce checkouts. No erroneous duplicate charges or double debits were reported. A small number of merchants (fewer than 20) contacted support regarding declined transactions; all were advised that the issue was under investigation and that retries would be required.

**3.2 Internal Impact**

The Payments service consumed 100% of its allocated database connection pool for a period of approximately 45 minutes. This caused a knock-on effect on the reporting and reconciliation jobs that share the same database cluster. These jobs were delayed by up to 90 minutes but completed without data loss. The internal admin portal also experienced intermittent timeouts during the peak of the incident.

**3.3 Data Integrity**

No data corruption or loss was identified. The transaction journal remained consistent. A post-incident reconciliation check (completed at 14:30 AEST) confirmed that all transactions processed before and after the incident are accounted for. No manual correction entries were required.

**4. TIMELINE OF EVENTS**

All times are AEST (UTC+10). The timeline below has been compiled from alert history, incident channel logs, and engineer notes. Times are approximate where noted.

**5. ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS (PRELIMINARY)**

The feature flag controlling the new code path was disabled at 10:47 AEST to mitigate the incident. The underlying code change has been reverted from the main branch pending further review and the addition of a database migration to create the required index.

| Review feature flag defaults in the release checklist | M. Chen | 2024-04-18 | Not started |
| Conduct a full post-incident review with the payments team | T. Nguyen | 2024-04-22 | Scheduled |

**8. POST-INCIDENT REVIEW NOTES**

The incident review will be held on 2024-04-22 at 14:00 AEST in the SRE meeting room (or via video conference for remote attendees). The agenda will cover the timeline, root cause, and action items listed above. All participants from the incident are expected to attend or provide written updates beforehand.

Payment Service has_incident_id INC-2024-04-15 identifier. Record status: historical.

Key discussion points to be covered:

- Whether the staging environment should more closely mirror production data volumes. The current staging database contains approximately 200,000 rows in the transactions table, which is not sufficient to expose query performance issues.
- Whether the deployment automation should require a manual confirmation step when a feature flag is set to "enabled" for 100% of traffic.
- Whether the SRE team should have visibility of the release notes for changes that affect database queries. Currently, the release notes are reviewed by the payments team only.
- Whether the alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation should be lowered to 70% to provide earlier warning.

**9. ATTACHMENTS**

| Attachment 2: Query plan analysis (10:23 AEST) | Output from the database team's investigation |

| Attachment 4: Connection pool utilisation graph | Screenshot from the metrics dashboard |

**10. INCIDENT IDENTIFIER**

This incident has been recorded in the incident management system under the identifier INC-2024-04-15. All related documentation, alert history, and communication logs should reference this identifier when filing follow-up work or when querying the incident history. The incident record is accessible to all SRE team members and to the payments team leadership. The identifier has been used in the action items above where applicable, and the post-incident review minutes will reference it as well.

documents.title: Incident Report: Payment Service Outage
documents.content:
**10. INCIDENT IDENTIFIER** (continued)

The incident identifier INC-2024-04-15 has been propagated to the following systems: the alert management platform (alert group `payments-prod`), the change management record associated with release v2.14.1, and the on-call handover notes for the week commencing 15 April 2024. Any future correspondence regarding this incident should include the identifier in the subject line.

**11. POST-INCIDENT REVIEW MINUTES**

The post-incident review was held on 18 April 2024, 10:00–11:30 AEST, via video conference. Attendees: J. Okafor (Incident Commander), M. Tran (SRE Lead), A. Patel (Database Team), S. Nguyen (Payments Engineering), R. Whitfield (QA), and L. Chen (Product). The following minutes were recorded.

**11.1 Review of timeline**

The group confirmed the timeline as documented in Section 4. No discrepancies were raised. One attendee noted that the monitoring system's alert for connection pool utilisation fired at 09:41 AEST, which is approximately one minute after the pool reached saturation. The alert was acknowledged at 09:47 AEST by the on-call engineer.

**11.2 Root cause discussion**

The database team presented the query plan analysis (Attachment 2). The plan confirmed that the new query in release v2.14.1 performed a full table scan on the `transactions` table. The table contains approximately 4.8 million rows in production. The query was executed on every request when the feature flag was enabled, and the execution time was measured at 3.2 seconds under normal load. The connection pool had a maximum of 50 connections, and each request held a connection for the duration of the query. At the time of the incident, the pool was exhausted within 90 seconds of the flag being enabled.

The discussion then turned to the staging environment. The current staging database contains approximately 200,000 rows in the transactions table, which is not sufficient to expose query performance issues. The team agreed that this is a contributing factor to the lack of detection during pre-release testing.

**11.3 Feature flag process**

The deployment automation for release v2.14.1 was configured to set the feature flag to "enabled" for 100% of traffic as the default. The team discussed whether the automation should require a manual confirmation step when a feature flag is set to "enabled" for 100% of traffic. No decision was reached, but the action item was recorded as ACTION-5.

**11.4 Release notes visibility**

The payments team noted that the release notes for v2.14.1 were reviewed internally but were not shared with the SRE team. The release notes contained a description of the new query and its expected behaviour. The SRE team requested visibility of release notes for changes that affect database queries. The payments team agreed to circulate release notes to the SRE team for such changes. This will be tracked under ACTION-6.

**11.5 Alerting threshold**

The current alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation is 80%. The SRE team proposed lowering the threshold to 70% to provide earlier warning. The payments team expressed concern that a lower threshold might generate noise during normal peak usage. The matter was deferred to a follow-up meeting. The alerting threshold for connection pool utilisation is currently configured at 80% and no change has been applied as of the date of these minutes.

**11.6 Action items**

**12. LESSONS LEARNED**
